risks.note: The Company states it 'operates in a highly competitive environment characterised by digital disruption, platform-led competition and rapidly evolving consumer preferences'. As a master distributor it sits between brand owners and marketplaces, so platform-led competition and shifting consumer preference bear directly on its role; mitigation is stated only as operational efficiency, customer engagement, marketplace integration and service differentiation.
risks.risk: Competition risk - highly competitive, digitally disrupted marketplace

risks.note: Structural, and implied by the Company's own strategy text: it aims to 'strengthen our foothold in existing Carvaan markets' and is 'exploring opportunities to diversify our portfolio beyond Carvaan'. Until that diversification lands, revenue and marketplace relevance rest on one nostalgia-led product family, whose appeal is tied to a specific demographic and cultural niche.
risks.risk: Product / brand concentration around the Carvaan portfolio

risks.note: Named by the Company: 'Digidrive's performance remains linked to macroeconomic conditions including inflation, consumer demand, interest rates and procurement costs.' As a discretionary-consumer-electronics distributor, both demand and procurement cost move with the cycle, and the Company says it responds only with calibrated operational and financial strategies.
risks.risk: Economic risk - performance linked to macroeconomic conditions

risks.note: Named by the Company as a key risk. In a distribution model working capital sits in trade receivables from channel and marketplace counterparties; management is via credit evaluation procedures, customer assessments, credit limits and monitoring of receivable ageing and collection patterns.

Named by the Company as a key risk, mitigated through prudent treasury management, adequate liquidity buffers, regular cash-flow monitoring and access to banking and financial arrangements. Relevant because the MD&A states the Company does not have any borrowings, so operations are funded from internal liquidity rather than committed credit.

Named by the Company as a key risk: it 'continues to invest in technology infrastructure, platform upgrades and digital capabilities to remain aligned with changing consumer behaviour and evolving industry requirements'. The whole operating model - SAP-enabled ERP, marketplace integration, API-linked logistics - depends on staying current with a fast-moving e-commerce stack, and the mitigation is ongoing spend rather than a structural hedge.

Management explicitly flags in the MD&A outlook that 'evolving macroeconomic conditions, geopolitical developments, inflationary trends and regulatory changes... may influence consumer sentiment, supply chains and operating costs', and says it is balancing growth opportunities with risk management and capital discipline.
risks.risk: Macroeconomic, geopolitical, inflationary and regulatory change affecting demand, supply chains and costs

risks.note: Structural to the model as described: product access to consumers runs through 'leading digital marketplaces' and fulfilment through direct API integration with logistics partners. The Company's stated priorities - strengthening marketplace distribution capabilities and channel partnerships - underline that market access is intermediated by platforms it does not own, in an ecosystem the MD&A itself says is being reconfigured by quick commerce, D2C and ONDC.
risks.risk: Dependence on third-party e-commerce marketplaces and logistics partners for reach and fulfilment

sk.overview: India's organised retail comprises organised brick-and-mortar and e-commerce, with e-commerce the fastest-growing format. India retail was ~Rs 83 trillion in FY2025 (~21% organised) and is projected to reach Rs 123-135 trillion by FY2030. India e-commerce (including quick commerce) is ~Rs 6 trillion GMV (~US$70 billion) currently, projected to reach Rs 15-18 trillion (12-13% retail penetration) by FY2030.
